newsitem.title: UK: MGAM could lose big pensions contract -- FT.
newsitem.headline: MGAM could lose big pensions contract -- FT.

text.p: Troubled fund management company Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) is in danger of losing a 200 million stg mandate to manage pension funds for a London council, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
The report said that Westminster City Council was to ask other fund managers to tender for the contract to manage half of its 400 million stg pension fund.

The funds have been managed for the past two years by the head of MGAM's UK institutional business. The report said that this was the first indication that troubles in MGAM's unit trust arm could affect its far bigger UK institutional business.

MGAM parent Deutsche Morgan Grenfell last week sacrificed four key managers in an attempt to restore faith in a a group reeling from revelations of misvaluations in three of its funds and the sacking of fund manager Peter Young.

The discovery of misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of three MGAM funds last month. Trading resumed after Deutsche Bank stepped in with a 180 million stg cash injection.
The Financial Times said that Morgan Grenfell has also been accused by a Canadian firm of failing to honour an alleged commitment made by Young to invest C$20 million in the company.
It said the claim had been made by Ukraine Enterprise Corporation but that Morgan Grenfell denied it had any legal commitment to supply the money.
Young was dismissed on the grounds of alleged "gross misconduct". He is being investigated by Britain's Serious Fraud Office but has said he is not guilty of any crime and is being made a scapegoat.
